findings.reason: §5 must extend `budget_group` and `lane_context` (adding both to its write paths) or state why the existing per-wallet block cannot carry lane pressure, otherwise the codebase ends with two mechanisms reporting one account's pressure and `test_budget_group_declaration.py`'s `SOL_FAMILY_LANES` pins the old one.
findings.text: §5 states lane pressure "once per lane in a lanes block" and lists `reckon/crew/picker/snapshot.py`, `types.py`, `state.jinja` and `questions.jinja` as write paths, but the picker's lane-shaped blocks are already composed by `reckon/crew/picker/lane_context.py:515 build()` (`return_times`, `local_lane`) and the once-per-account quota position is already owned by `reckon/crew/budget_group.py:1` ("Quota positions read once per declared wallet, never per lane", with no per-backend entry point), and `Candidate.family` is already emitted as the `lane` field at `reckon/crew/picker/prompts.py:112` — so §5 as written adds a second lane-pressure path beside the two owners instead of extending them

findings.reason: each added family member must be accounted for in its own section's text (name the option/key retired or merged, or state why none can be); as written the cli_options count 323 and the definition count 1529 only grow.
findings.text: §4 adds `--model KEY` to `crew dispatch` and "its sibling surfaces that already take `--backend`" — the `--backend` option is declared at `reckon/cli.py:1788`, `:1891`, `:2688`, `:6685` and `:6779` — with no line stating which surface this retires or merges, and §1 adds a top-level `lanes:` key to the flight schema (new public definitions) and §7 adds a public `resolve_name` with no retirement named either

rubric_items.deep_module: pass — §7's single `resolve_name(name) -> (lane, model_key)` hides three stored vocabularies (backend name, model id, alias) behind one read-side resolver, and §1 hides the lane→backend expansion behind flight resolution, so both add depth rather than surface.
rubric_items.duplicate_owner: a finding — §5 re-implements the once-per-account pressure that `reckon/crew/budget_group.py` already owns and the picker lane block `reckon/crew/picker/lane_context.py:515` already composes.
rubric_items.interface_budget: a finding — public_definitions 1529, cli_options 323, mcp_views 33, refusal_families 23; §1, §4 and §7 add surface to these families without naming what each retires or merges, or why nothing can be.
rubric_items.reuse_search: pass — the plan names the mechanism it extends (the dialect-derived lane at `reckon/_backends.py:1945` `_DIALECTS` and `reckon/crew/picker/snapshot.py:415` `Candidate.family`) and the design report it was built from, rather than proposing a new axis.
rubric_items.thin_wrapper: pass — §4's `--model` is an orthogonal input beside `--backend` (a lane's default model is still taken with `--backend` alone), not a forwarding layer, and §7's resolver reads data the catalogue already holds rather than duplicating a mechanism.
